title: Rill and the Lake the Size of a Teacup
synopsis: On Rill’s first orchard visit, an ordinary puddle becomes Lake Teacup in the friends’ imagined Button Town.
continuity_state: Before: Rill has not visited the orchard; Nori’s boot-and-ripple drawing remains in Grandma Fern’s brown envelope at Blue Door Cottage; Button Town has no lake. After: Rill visits southern orchard with Aunt Cress and receives Nori’s picture, which Aunt Cress carries home. The friends name an ordinary shallow rain puddle Lake Teacup in their game; a separate blue-circle drawing stays at Blue Door Cottage for the future pretend map.

related_resources.reason: The simple real-place label is explicit before introducing a pretend role; the AAP report documents the broad value and forms of play, not this narration.
A familiar object takes a new imaginary role, consistent with play props described in Harvard’s age-banded guidance.
